/-!
# Banach's problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Stefan Banach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Banach)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace Banachs

open MeasureTheory

/--
Banach's problem asks whether there is an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation
of a standard probability space with simple Lebesgue spectrum. Here an invertible transformation
is presented as a measurable $\mathbb{Z}$-action `S`, with the transformation itself equal to
`S 1`. Simple Lebesgue spectrum on $L^2_0$ means that there is an $f$ whose two-sided Koopman
orbit $f \circ S_n$ is orthonormal and has closed complex linear span equal to the orthogonal
complement of the constant functions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 28 37 47]
theorem banachs :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ X : Type, ∃ m : MeasurableSpace X, letI := m
      ∃ sb : StandardBorelSpace X, letI := sb
      ∃ μ : Measure X, ∃ pm : IsProbabilityMeasure μ, letI := pm
      ∃ S : ℤ → X ≃ᵐ X,
      ∃ hS : ∀ n, MeasurePreserving (S n) μ μ,
        S 0 = MeasurableEquiv.refl X ∧
        (∀ a b, S (a + b) = (S a).trans (S b)) ∧
        Ergodic (S 1) μ ∧
        ∃ f : Lp ℂ 2 μ,
          Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : ℤ => Lp.compMeasurePreserving (S n) (hS n) f) ∧
          (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (fun n : ℤ =>
            Lp.compMeasurePreserving (S n) (hS n) f))).topologicalClosure =
            ((Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (Lp.const 2 μ : ℂ →+ Lp ℂ 2 μ))) :
              Submodule ℂ (Lp ℂ 2 μ))ᗮ := by
  sorry

end Banachs
modeling_decisions: Used the standard probability-space convention from the decomposition: an arbitrary probability measure on a standard Borel space.

Modeled an invertible measure-preserving transformation by a measurable measure-preserving ℤ-action S, with the transformation T = S 1. This supplies the two-sided iterates despite Mathlib having no integer-power API for MeasurableEquiv.
Used the equivalent cyclic-orbit characterization of simple Lebesgue spectrum: there is f whose Koopman orbit n ↦ f ∘ S n is orthonormal and whose closed complex linear span is L²₀.
Represented L²₀ as the orthogonal complement in Lp ℂ 2 μ of the complex constant functions, namely the span of the range of Lp.const. This excludes the constant eigenfunction.
Used the Koopman convention U_T f = f ∘ T, as specified in the decomposition.

      (μ : ProbabilityMeasure X) (T : X ≃ᵐ X),
      Ergodic T (μ : Measure X) ∧
      ∃ (hpow : ∀ n : ℤ,
          MeasurePreserving ((T.toEquiv ^ n : Equiv.Perm X) : X → X) (μ : Measure X) μ)
        (b : HilbertBasis ℤ ℂ ((ℂ ∙ Lp.const 2 (μ : Measure X) (1 : ℂ))ᗮ)),
        ∀ n : ℤ,
          (b n).1 =
            Lp.compMeasurePreserving (E := ℂ) (p := 2) (μ := (μ : Measure X))
              (μb := (μ : Measure X)) ((T.toEquiv ^ n : Equiv.Perm X) : X → X) (hpow n)
              (b 0 : Lp ℂ 2 (μ : Measure X)) := by
  sorry

end Banachs

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Banach's problem

Is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

In Banach's original formulation (recorded in Ulam's book, see below) the question asks for a
measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a square integrable function $f$ such that the
functions $f \circ T^n$ form a complete orthonormal system. In its modern form the question
asks for an ergodic automorphism $T$ of a standard probability space $(X, \mu)$ whose Koopman
operator $U_T f = f \circ T$ has simple Lebesgue spectrum on the orthocomplement $L^2_0(X, \mu)$
of the constants, i.e. such that there is $f \in L^2_0(X, \mu)$ for which
$\{U_T^n f : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(X, \mu)$. This is the
formulation formalised here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Dynamical_systems)
- [Wikipedia, Stefan Banach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Banach)
- S. M. Ulam, *Problems in Modern Mathematics*, Wiley, New York, 1964.
- M. Lemańczyk, *Spectral theory of dynamical systems*, in: Encyclopedia of Complexity and
  Systems Science, Springer, 2009.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace Banachs

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X}

/--
The **Koopman operator** $U_T f = f \circ T$ of a measure-preserving measurable equivalence
$T$ of $(X, \mu)$, as a unitary operator (a linear isometry equivalence) of
$L^2(X, \mu; \mathbb{C})$.
-/
noncomputable def koopman (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    Lp ℂ 2 μ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ where
  toLinearEquiv :=
    { Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T hT with
      invFun := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T.symm (hT.symm T)
      left_inv := fun g => by
        apply Lp.ext
        refine (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).trans ?_
        refine ((hT.symm T).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
          (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving g hT)).trans ?_
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by simp
      right_inv := fun g => by
        apply Lp.ext
        refine (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).trans ?_
        refine (hT.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
          (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving g (hT.symm T))).trans ?_
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by simp }
  norm_map' g := Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving g hT

/-- The Koopman operator acts by $f \mapsto f \circ T$ (almost everywhere). -/
@[category API, AMS 37 47]
lemma koopman_apply_ae_eq (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    koopman T hT f =ᵐ[μ] f ∘ T :=
  Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT

/-- The inverse of the Koopman operator of $T$ is the Koopman operator of $T^{-1}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 37 47]
lemma koopman_symm (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    (koopman T hT).symm = koopman T.symm (hT.symm T) :=
  rfl

@[category test, AMS 37 47]
lemma koopman_refl : koopman (MeasurableEquiv.refl X) (MeasurePreserving.id μ) = 1 := by
  ext f
  exact (koopman_apply_ae_eq _ _ f).trans (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => rfl)

/-- The Koopman operator fixes the constant functions. -/
@[category test, AMS 37 47]
lemma koopman_const [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ)
    (c : ℂ) : koopman T hT (Lp.const 2 μ c) = Lp.const 2 μ c := by
  apply Lp.ext
  refine (koopman_apply_ae_eq T hT _).trans ?_
  refine (hT.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp (Lp.coeFn_const 2 μ c)).trans ?_
  exact (Lp.coeFn_const 2 μ c).symm

/--
**Banach's problem.** Is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

That is, is there an ergodic automorphism $T$ (an invertible measure-preserving transformation
with measurable inverse) of a standard probability space $(X, \mu)$ whose Koopman operator
$U_T f = f \circ T$ has simple Lebesgue spectrum on $L^2_0(X, \mu)$, the orthocomplement of the
constants in $L^2(X, \mu; \mathbb{C})$? Equivalently: is there $f \in L^2(X, \mu; \mathbb{C})$
whose orbit $\{U_T^n f : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(X, \mu)$, i.e.
it is orthonormal and its closed linear span is $L^2_0(X, \mu)$? (Such an $f$ automatically
lies in $L^2_0(X, \mu)$.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 47]
theorem banachs :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (X : Type) (_ : MeasurableSpace X) (_ : StandardBorelSpace X) (μ : Measure X)
        (_ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : Ergodic T μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ),
        Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : ℤ => (koopman T hT.toMeasurePreserving ^ n) f) ∧
        (Submodule.span ℂ
          (Set.range fun n : ℤ => (koopman T hT.toMeasurePreserving ^ n) f)).topologicalClosure =
            (ℂ ∙ Lp.const 2 μ (1 : ℂ))ᗮ := by
  sorry

end Banachs

modeling_decisions: Convention: the modern finite-measure formulation is used — a standard Borel probability space (`StandardBorelSpace X`, `IsProbabilityMeasure μ`) rather than Banach's original σ-finite setting (Lebesgue measure on ℝ). Correspondingly 'spectrum' is taken on L²₀ = orthocomplement of the constants (`(ℂ ∙ Lp.const 2 μ 1)ᗮ`), so the trivial constant eigenfunction is excluded, as in the decomposition notes.

The system is an invertible ℤ-action: `T : X ≃ᵐ X` (a measurable equivalence that is measure preserving via `Ergodic`), i.e. a genuine Borel automorphism rather than an invertible-mod-0 map; on standard Borel spaces every mod-0 automorphism agrees a.e. with a Borel automorphism, so the existence question is unaffected.

'Simple Lebesgue spectrum' is formalized by its standard equivalent characterization: there is f whose ℤ-orbit {U_T^n f} is orthonormal with closed linear span equal to L²₀ (a Hilbert basis of L²₀). This avoids spectral measures/maximal spectral type, which Mathlib lacks. `f ∈ L²₀` is not stated separately because it follows (f = U_T^0 f lies in the closed span).
Ergodicity uses Mathlib's `Ergodic` (measure preserving + every strictly invariant measurable set is null or conull), which is the standard notion for measure-preserving maps.
Scalars are ℂ (`Lp ℂ 2 μ`), the standard setting for spectral theory of Koopman operators; the inner product is the L² inner product (`L2.innerProductSpace`).
The existential quantifies over `X : Type` (universe 0); every standard Borel space is Borel-isomorphic to a Borel subset of ℝ, so this loses no generality.

`answer(True)` corresponds to a positive answer (such a system exists), `answer(False)` to a negative one. Degenerate witnesses are impossible: an ergodic system with atoms is finite, so L² is finite-dimensional and cannot contain a ℤ-indexed orthonormal family.

Including `StandardBorelSpace X` follows the standard phrasing 'standard probability space'; since simple Lebesgue spectrum forces L² to be separable, the answer is the same with or without this hypothesis.
Per the task constraints, the bespoke `koopman` definition lives in the problem file rather than `FormalConjecturesForMathlib`; a reviewer may wish to move it there (it is generic and fully proved).

The problem goes back to Banach and is recorded in Ulam's *A Collection of Mathematical
Problems*: does there exist a square integrable function $f$ and a measure-preserving
transformation $T$ such that the functions $f \circ T^n$ form a complete orthonormal system?

In its modern form the question asks whether there is an ergodic automorphism $T$ of a standard
probability space $(X, \mu)$ whose Koopman operator $U_T f = f \circ T$, restricted to the
orthocomplement $L^2_0(\mu)$ of the constants, has simple Lebesgue spectrum, i.e. its maximal
spectral type is Lebesgue measure on the circle and its multiplicity is one. Equivalently, the
restriction of $U_T$ to $L^2_0(\mu)$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $z$ on
$L^2(\mathbb{T}, \mathrm{Leb})$, i.e. there is $f \in L^2_0(\mu)$ such that
$\{U_T^n f : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(\mu)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stefan Banach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Banach)
- S. M. Ulam, *A Collection of Mathematical Problems*, Interscience Publishers, New York, 1960.
- M. Lemańczyk, *Spectral theory of dynamical systems*, in: Encyclopedia of Complexity and
  Systems Science, Springer, 2009.

open MeasureTheory

namespace Banachs

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X}

/-- The **Koopman operator** `f ↦ f ∘ T` on `L²(μ)` associated to a measure-preserving
measurable equivalence `T`, as a unitary operator (a linear isometric equivalence). Its inverse
is `f ↦ f ∘ T⁻¹`. -/
noncomputable def koopman (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    Lp ℂ 2 μ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ where
  toLinearEquiv :=
    { Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T hT with
      invFun := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T.symm hT.symm
      left_inv := fun f => Lp.ext <|
        (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ hT.symm).trans <|
          (hT.symm.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
            (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT)).trans <|
          Filter.EventuallyEq.of_eq <| by
            rw [Function.comp_assoc, MeasurableEquiv.self_comp_symm, Function.comp_id]
      right_inv := fun f => Lp.ext <|
        (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ hT).trans <|
          (hT.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
            (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT.symm)).trans <|
          Filter.EventuallyEq.of_eq <| by
            rw [Function.comp_assoc, MeasurableEquiv.symm_comp_self, Function.comp_id] }
  norm_map' f := Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving f hT

@[category API, AMS 28 37]
lemma koopman_apply (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    koopman T hT f =ᵐ[μ] f ∘ T :=
  Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT

@[category API, AMS 28 37]
lemma koopman_symm_apply (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    (koopman T hT).symm f =ᵐ[μ] f ∘ T.symm :=
  Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT.symm

/-- A measure-preserving measurable equivalence `T` of a finite measure space `(X, μ)` has
**simple Lebesgue spectrum** (on the orthocomplement of the constants) if there is
`f ∈ L²(μ)` such that the two-sided orbit `{U_T ^ n f : n ∈ ℤ}` of `f` under the Koopman
operator `U_T` is an orthonormal basis of the closed subspace `L²₀(μ) = {1}ᗮ` of `L²(μ)`
orthogonal to the constant functions (necessarily `f ∈ L²₀(μ)`). This is equivalent to the
restriction of `U_T` to `L²₀(μ)` being unitarily equivalent to the bilateral shift, i.e. to
multiplication by `z` on `L²(𝕋, Leb)`: its maximal spectral type is Lebesgue measure and its
spectral multiplicity is one. -/
def HasSimpleLebesgueSpectrum [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    Prop :=
  ∃ f : Lp ℂ 2 μ,
    Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : ℤ => (koopman T hT ^ n) f) ∧

/-!
# Banach's problem

Banach asked whether there is an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum. In its
original form (recorded by Ulam) the question asks for a measure-preserving transformation
$T$ of the real line and a square-integrable function $f$ such that the functions
$f \circ T^n$ form a complete orthonormal system in $L^2$. In modern language, the problem is
whether an ergodic (invertible) measure-preserving transformation $T$ of a standard probability
space $(X, \mu)$ can have simple Lebesgue spectrum: the Koopman operator $U_T f = f \circ T$,
restricted to the orthogonal complement $L^2_0(\mu)$ of the constant functions, is unitarily
equivalent to multiplication by $z$ on $L^2$ of the unit circle with Lebesgue measure.
Equivalently, there is $f \in L^2_0(\mu)$ such that $\{U_T^n f : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(\mu)$.

The problem is open. It is listed among the unsolved problems in dynamical systems on
Wikipedia.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Stefan Banach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Banach)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ul60] Ulam, S. M. *Problems in Modern Mathematics*. Wiley, 1960.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace Banachs

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X}

/-- The Koopman operator $U_T f = f \circ T$ of an invertible measure-preserving transformation
`T`, as a unitary operator on the complex Hilbert space $L^2(\mu)$. -/
noncomputable def koopman (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    Lp ℂ 2 μ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ where
  toLinearEquiv :=
    { Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T hT with
      invFun := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗ ℂ T.symm (hT.symm T)
      left_inv := fun g => by
        apply Lp.ext
        refine (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).trans ?_
        refine ((hT.symm T).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
          (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving g hT)).trans ?_
        filter_upwards with x
        simp
      right_inv := fun g => by
        apply Lp.ext
        refine (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).trans ?_
        refine (hT.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
          (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving g (hT.symm T))).trans ?_
        filter_upwards with x
        simp }
  norm_map' g := Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving g hT

@[category API, AMS 37 47]
theorem koopman_apply_ae (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    koopman T hT f =ᵐ[μ] f ∘ T :=
  Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT

@[category API, AMS 37 47]
theorem koopman_symm (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ) :
    (koopman T hT).symm = koopman T.symm (hT.symm T) :=
  rfl

@[category API, AMS 37 47]
theorem koopman_zpow_neg_one_apply_ae (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : MeasurePreserving T μ μ)
    (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    (koopman T hT ^ (-1 : ℤ)) f =ᵐ[μ] f ∘ T.symm := by
  rw [zpow_neg_one]
  exact Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f (hT.symm T)

theorem koopman_trans (S T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hS : MeasurePreserving S μ μ)

    koopman S hS (koopman T hT f) = koopman (S.trans T) (hT.comp hS) f := by
  apply Lp.ext
  refine (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).trans ?_
  refine (hS.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f hT)).trans ?_
  exact (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving _ _).symm

/--
**Banach's problem.** Is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

That is, is there a standard probability space $(X, \mu)$ and an invertible measure-preserving
transformation $T$ of $X$ that is ergodic and whose Koopman operator $U_T f = f \circ T$ has

of $U_T$ with eigenvalue $1$, so $U_T$ itself can never have Lebesgue spectrum on $L^2(\mu)$ of
a probability space.
-/

      ∃ (X : Type) (_ : MeasurableSpace X) (_ : StandardBorelSpace X) (μ : Measure X)

        Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : ℤ => (koopman T hT.toMeasurePreserving ^ n) f) ∧
        (Submodule.span ℂ

            (ℂ ∙ Lp.const 2 μ (1 : ℂ))ᗮ := by
  sorry

end Banachs

    Lp ℂ 2 μ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℂ T hT) fun g =>
    ⟨Lp.compMeasurePreserving T.symm (hT.symm T) g, by
      apply Lp.ext
      have h₁ := Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving (Lp.compMeasurePreserving T.symm (hT.symm T) g) hT
      have h₂ :=
        hT.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving g (hT.symm T))
      refine (h₁.trans h₂).trans ?_
      filter_upwards with x
      simp⟩

    apply (koopman T hT).injective
    rw [LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    apply Lp.ext
    have h₁ := Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving (Lp.compMeasurePreserving T.symm (hT.symm T) f) hT

    filter_upwards with x
    simp

  exact Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving f (hT.symm T)

/-- **Banach's problem**: is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

That is, is there an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation `T` of a standard
probability space `(X, μ)` whose Koopman operator $U_T$ has simple Lebesgue spectrum on the
orthocomplement $L^2_0(\mu)$ of the constants: is there $f \in L^2_0(\mu)$ such that the orbit

An orthonormal orbit $(U_T^n f)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ means that the spectral measure of $f$ is
Lebesgue measure on the circle, and the orbit spanning $L^2_0(\mu)$ means that $f$ is a cyclic
vector. So this is the same as $U_T$ restricted to $L^2_0(\mu)$ being unitarily equivalent to
multiplication by $z$ on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, i.e. having Lebesgue maximal spectral type with
multiplicity one. Since Lebesgue spectrum on $L^2_0(\mu)$ has no eigenvalues, ergodicity is
implied, but it is part of the question as stated. -/

    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (X : Type) (_ : MeasurableSpace X) (_ : StandardBorelSpace X) (μ : Measure X)
        (_ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (T : X ≃ᵐ X) (hT : Ergodic T μ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 μ)
        (b : HilbertBasis ℤ ℂ (ℂ ∙ Lp.const 2 μ (1 : ℂ))ᗮ),
        ∀ n : ℤ, (b n : Lp ℂ 2 μ) = (koopman T hT.toMeasurePreserving ^ n) f := by
